rewrite: Urban heat islands threaten public health and raise energy use in tropical cities. This paper examines how green space coverage relates to surface temperature in Kota Mangrove Jaya. We analyzed Landsat imagery from 2015 to 2025 across 74 administrative villages. Every 10 percent increase in vegetation cover corresponded to a 1.4 degree Celsius drop in average land surface temperature. Villages with less than 5 percent green space reached peak temperatures of 41.8 degrees Celsius in the dry season. The pattern is largely explained by rice fields being replaced with asphalt and metal roofing, which absorb and re-radiate heat. A household survey of 320 respondents found that residents of the hottest areas spent 27 percent more on electricity for cooling. The findings support building green infrastructure into urban planning, and give policymakers evidence for making cities more resilient and livable.

Hi team, the release of Orbit Planner 3.0 has moved from 5 October to 19 October 2026. During final testing, QA found that calendar sync failed for roughly 8 percent of Outlook users, which would have affected about 12,000 accounts. To give engineering time to fix it, we are freezing all new feature work from this Wednesday. Marketing assets must now be final by 14 October. The press embargo lifts at 9:00 a.m. Jakarta time on launch day. Legal has asked that "no screenshots showing customer names appear in any external material." Thanks for your work. Best regards, Daniel Hartono, Product Lead, Brightpath Software.

Dear Ms. Wulandari, I am following up on the delayed shipment under purchase order PO-2026-0917. As discussed on our call, Kalimaya Textiles expected 2,400 meters of cotton fabric by 10 September 2026. The goods have not yet arrived at our warehouse in Cikarang Barat. The delay is serious because our production line has been idle for four days, costing us an estimated Rp 38 million in lost output. We value our long partnership. However, clause 7 of our agreement states that "late deliveries exceeding ten days incur a 2 percent penalty per week." We therefore ask for a confirmed delivery date by the end of this Friday. If the shipment is split, please send the 800 meters of navy fabric for our export order first. Kind regards, Bayu Pratama, Procurement Manager.

The Aurora Desk Lamp has 5 color temperatures, from 2700K to 6500K, so you can shift from warm evening light to crisp daylight. A built-in ambient sensor adjusts brightness automatically, which reduces eye strain during long evening work sessions. The body is recycled aluminum. It weighs 1.1 kilograms and feels sturdy. A USB-C port on the base charges your phone at up to 20 watts. In a study of 150 remote workers in Bandung, 78 percent reported fewer headaches after two weeks of use. Every lamp comes with a 3-year warranty and ships free across Indonesia within 4 business days. Designed by Lumos Home Studio, the Aurora is available now for Rp 749,000.

NestNote is a family planner that puts chores, meals, and schedules in one app. Since its launch in April 2025, more than 60,000 families across Southeast Asia have used it to coordinate them. The shared calendar syncs in real time across up to 8 family members, so everyone sees the same plan. The grocery list groups items by aisle, which helped beta users cut average shopping trips from 52 minutes to 31 minutes. Parents can set screen-time rewards that unlock when kids finish assigned tasks. NestNote stores all data on servers in Singapore and never sells personal information. Premium costs USD 3.99 per month, with a 30-day free trial for new users. A reviewer from Penang said the app finally ended the era of the family whiteboard. Download NestNote today.

The Sulawesi Rail Authority announced on Thursday, 17 September 2026, that the Makassar-Parepare line will add six new daily trips from 1 November. Daily capacity is expected to rise from 4,200 to 7,800 passengers. Authority director Hasanuddin Baso said the decision followed a surge in ridership after Barru Timur station opened in March. Weekend trains had been running at 112 percent of seated capacity, he said, forcing many passengers to stand for more than two hours. Four additional train sets, leased from a domestic manufacturer for Rp 64 billion, will run the new schedule. "Every new train set must meet the accessibility standard for wheelchair users," Baso told a press conference. Local business groups welcomed the move and said it could bring more tourists to the western coast. Some commuters worry that fares may rise next year. The expansion is a step toward a more integrated transport network in the region.

AquaSense Labs, a startup from Kendari, won the top prize at the 2026 Indonesia Green Innovation Awards for a low-cost sensor that detects heavy metal contamination in drinking water within 15 minutes. The award, presented in Jakarta on 8 September, includes a Rp 750 million grant to scale up production. Founder Nadia Kusumawati said the idea came after a 2024 survey found unsafe lead levels in 31 of 90 village wells near nickel processing sites. Laboratory testing costs about Rp 1.2 million per sample and takes up to three weeks, which is why most villages never test at all, she said. Each AquaSense unit costs Rp 450,000 and can be reused for about 200 tests. The judges called it "practical enough for a village health volunteer to operate alone." The company plans to distribute 1,000 units across Southeast Sulawesi by mid-2027. The win shows the potential of homegrown innovation.

A landslide on Monday cut off the only road between Kampung Lembah Hijau and the district capital. It struck at about 3:40 a.m., after two days of torrential rain dropped 186 millimeters on the area. The local disaster agency said mud and fallen trees buried a 70-meter stretch of road. Officials said illegal logging upstream had weakened the slope by removing much of the vegetation that holds the soil in place. About 1,350 residents are isolated, and volunteers are carrying emergency food in on foot. Agency head Yulius Kambuaya said "heavy equipment must reach the site within 48 hours to prevent food shortages." Two excavators were sent on Tuesday morning, 22 September 2026, but continued rain has slowed their progress. No casualties have been reported so far. Authorities have pledged to investigate the logging in the watershed.

Is remote work here to stay? The pandemic changed how we think about the workplace, but the evidence since then is more mixed than either enthusiasts or skeptics suggest. A 2026 survey by the Meridian Workforce Institute found that 58 percent of Indonesian office workers prefer a hybrid schedule of two or three office days. Only 12 percent wanted to work fully from home, largely because cramped housing makes a quiet workspace hard to find. In my view, this points to something policy debates often overlook: remote work is only as good as the home it happens in. The Jakarta-based firm Kirana Analytics responded by paying a monthly allowance of Rp 500,000 for co-working spaces. Its policy states that "no employee should have to work from a bedroom unless they choose to." Flexibility without support only transfers the costs. The future of work has to be built around people, not just places.

Few topics in education are debated as much as standardized testing. For decades, exams have been treated as a fair and objective way to measure student achievement. But it is worth asking what these tests measure and what they leave out. In the province of Sulawesi Raya, 2025 national exam results showed 67 percent of students in urban schools passed mathematics, against 34 percent in rural schools. That gap, I would argue, says more about access to trained teachers than about student ability. According to the Provincial Education Office, rural districts there have one certified mathematics teacher for every 210 students. Some schools have tried portfolio assessment. Sekolah Alam Tepian Danau reported a 22 percent rise in attendance after dropping weekly drill tests. Its principal put it simply: "we grade the project, not the panic." Tests will not disappear overnight, nor should they. Assessment needs a balanced approach so that it serves learning.
